quotes.text: Efforts in Michigan to regulate artificial intelligence in elections are in the early stage, but the new laws represent a start, state Senate Elections Chair Jeremy Moss (D) said in an interview. “We’re trying to clamp down on what has been threatened to happen,” said Moss.

@votepenelope @JocelynBenson @Promote_VoteMI @DETROITNAACP @NotPoliticians @GovWhitmer Strengthening election administration

• Process absentee ballots before Election Day

• Protect election workers from harassment

Preventing attacks on election systems

• Clarify how electors convene after election (no fake slates!)

• Restrict AI ads/ban deep fakes

Our Democratic majority passed and I voted for the strongest regulations around data centers of any state in the country. Our law protects our water supply and ensures that the cost of data centers are not burdened on us as ratepayers. I support local input and control as these proposals pop up in Michigan communities.

These are the people who are working to eliminate our jobs and force data centers on every community in MI," Moss said in a social media post. "They know they can buy Jeremy. Bring it on, billionaires.

AI policy is at a volatile crossroads and industry insiders are raising the alarm bells of what’s ahead. We can either put our heads in the sand or create strong, durable guardrails. Congressional Republicans have made their choice: they’re on a months-long recess. 

We must elect a Congress that will put the work in to implement regulations that will rein in rogue AI development and hold the companies legally accountable for harm before it’s too late.
